utterances.text: Yes. We've slipped backwards and forwards between masterful and powerful. It may be it's going -- translating backwards and forwards and we're getting a different word back. Your Honour, this is why I wanted to explore it in these terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: However this word is coming across to you, Mr. Radic, in your own language, in -- you won't hear this, but it's -- there's a phrase in English which is now being translated for you, "masterful leader". And that's coming across to your in your own language. And whatever the phrase is that's coming across to you in your own language, I just want to clarify that you intended it and you intend it as a description of Mr. Krajisnik in a positive, complimentary sense; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said a moment ago that he was a respected president of the National Assembly of Republika Srpska. In our language, a leader has a completely different meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, would you please check in the B/C/S original what word is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's exactly what we're doing. Because this is precisely the purpose of this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then perhaps you would ask Ms. Cmeric to read exactly the part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour read our minds here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And again, could you indicate it to the English text where exactly, what page we have to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. What would do, Your Honour, and Mr. Radic, so that you know, Ms. Cmeric is going to read just the relevant few lines, which you can also, I hope, follow. I'm not sure. Has Mr. Radic got at the moment, physically got a B/C/S version? No, he hasn't, has he? We have a spare, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in the English version --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then Ms. Cmeric can perhaps give us also the page reference in the English version so that everybody can follow it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, it's the 2001 or the 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: 62, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 62. Thank you, Ms. Cmeric.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That matches my note, Your Honour. Yes, it will be page 62 and 63 of the 2001 interview. And it's at the bottom -- or towards the bottom of page 62. It starts -- we're starting at line 30: "And if they have ...". That's the English phrase: "And if they have ..." And Ms. Cmeric is going to give us the Serbian version of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now that they have skilful leader like Krajisnik, then that's why I tell you - excuse me -

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who has a skilful leader? Mr. Radic: Answer: The deputies. He was their president. [Previous translation continues]... you would like me to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to verify with the interpreters that where in writing we have what was just read as masterful leader, where it's now translated as skilful. Do the interpreters competent in those languages agree that it should be skilful rather than masterful?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word vjesto is skilful. Of course, you can take it a step further and use a different word and maybe use masterful, but vjesto, basic meaning skilful there. Thank you very much for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is most helpful. INTERPRETER: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry. Your Honour, that's extremely helpful. We have been slightly troubled by this translation all the way along and of course what we -- what would have happened at the original interview, Ms. Korner -- it was Ms. Korner, I think, Ms. Korner speaking in English, she would have received an English translation picked up the word from the English translation offered to her and it goes backwards and forwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least we have now a proper translation of at least the words used by this witness during that interview, because I take it that the B/C/S correctly transcribes what he said. At least we have no reason to -- at this moment to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's a quarter to 2.00. Mr. Radic, we'll finish if the day, but we're not ready yet. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom. May I again instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given yesterday and today and the testimony you're still about to give tomorrow. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom. And then, Mr. Stewart, perhaps you could already prepare for an answer, but the question I put to Mr. Tieger will be the next question put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is, about tomorrow and about time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I expect to come in comfortably within the guideline. That's the first answer to Your Honour's question. The second, more specific answer to Your Honour's question is that I am confident, we give confidence rather than guarantees, Your Honour, as everybody will appreciate, I'm confident of finishing before the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Then I have one other issue, Mr. Stewart. I meanwhile read the -- perhaps I should -- no. I think I should go into private session just for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of October 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
